en.intro: Krishna has just exposed the limits of the ritual path. Now he makes a direct promise to those who turn to him with undivided attention.
en.notice: The word ananyah means with no other focus, and Krishna promises to personally carry the welfare and security of those who keep their mind on him alone.
en.next: He then addresses those who worship other radiant beings and says they still end up worshipping him, but in the wrong way.
en.meaning: Those who think of me alone and worship me with unwavering focus, I carry their welfare and security.

hi.intro: कृष्ण ने अभी कर्मकांड का मार्ग बताया है। अब वे उस व्यक्ति से एक सीधा वचन देते हैं जो अपना ध्यान केवल उन्हीं पर लगाता है।
hi.meaning: जो अनन्य भक्त मेरा चिन्तन करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं, मेरेमें निरन्तर लगे हुए उन भक्तोंका योगक्षेम अप्राप्तकी प्राप्ति और प्राप्तकी रक्षा मैं वहन करता हूँ ॥
hi.notice: अनन्याः, यानी जिनका कोई दूसरा लक्ष्य नहीं है, यह शब्द उन भक्तों को दर्शाता है जिनका ध्यान केवल कृष्ण पर है और कृष्ण उनके लिए योगक्षेम वहन करते हैं।
hi.next: वे फिर उन लोगों की ओर मुड़ते हैं जो अन्य देवताओं की पूजा करते हैं और कहते हैं कि वे भी अंततः उनकी ही पूजा कर रहे हैं, पर गलत तरीके से।

en.intro: Krishna has just exposed the limits of the ritual path. Now he makes a direct promise to those who turn to him with undivided attention.
en.body: Those who think of me alone and worship me with unwavering focus, I carry their welfare and security. The word ananyah means with no other focus, and Krishna promises to personally carry the welfare and security of those who keep their mind on him alone. He then addresses those who worship other radiant beings and says they still end up worshipping him, but in the wrong way.

issues: wrong_fact: "The word ananyah means with no other focus, and it marks the line between those who seek many heavens and those who seek only the one." (The intro and notice claim Krishna 'answers a question' about what happens to the person who gives up all other paths. However, the source verse 22 is a direct promise to the devotee, not an answer to a question. Furthermore, the notice claims the verse 'marks the line between those who seek many heavens and those who seek only the one,' which is a conceptual interpretation, not the literal meaning of the word ananyah or the content of this specific verse.)

wrong_fact: "Krishna then turns to those who worship other gods and says they still end up worshipping him, but in the wrong way." (This describes the content of verse 23, not verse 22. The 'next' field in the script misdescribes the immediate next verse as being about those who worship other gods, when the actual next verse (verse 23) is about those who worship other radiant beings. More importantly, the 'intro' and 'notice' misstate the context by suggesting verse 22 is a direct answer to a question about abandoning all other paths, which contradicts the source text's presentation of verse 22 as a standalone promise.)
